Greybeard found no matching confirmed guidance, so there is no memory ID or prior rollout experience to apply. I also have no live tenant connection; current policies, device inventory, compliance results, ownership, and exceptions are unavailable evidence.

Windows compliance plan:

1. Define scope: supported Windows editions/builds, corporate vs. BYOD, user groups, critical apps, and regulatory requirements.
2. Baseline controls: require supported OS versions, Secure Boot, TPM, BitLocker, firewall, antivirus/EDR, current threat intelligence, password/PIN standards, and acceptable device-risk levels.
3. Establish remediation: grace periods, user notifications, self-service instructions, help-desk escalation, documented exceptions, and time-limited waivers.
4. Pilot safely: start with IT and representative business users; use report-only or non-blocking evaluation before enforcing access restrictions.
5. Validate: measure enrollment coverage, false positives, remediation time, application compatibility, and support volume.
6. Roll out in rings: pilot, early adopters, departments, then broad deployment, with rollback criteria for each ring.
7. Operate continuously: review failures, exceptions, ownership, policy drift, OS lifecycle dates, and monthly compliance trends.

Missing local rollout knowledge: management platform/configuration, existing baselines, device population, deployment rings, maintenance windows, application dependencies, support capacity, exception owners, risk appetite, and approved enforcement dates.
